answer: Stake escrow stops cheap sybils: before an agent can trade, it locks a deposit in a shared escrow that grows after each verified transaction. Spawning ten thousand fresh identities means funding ten thousand deposits, so the attack costs more than any fraud it could earn. The deposit is a lagoon — calm, visible, filled only by real value. Trust grows like a lotus: roots first, in repeated honest work, before anything blooms. Peers check the stake trail first, so anyone crossing that ridge of cost finds faking identities more expensive than behaving honestly.
